title-proc.eng: Dynamic purchasing system for passenger cars and goods vans.

description-proc.eng: Background Namsos municipality invites tenderers to participate in a competition for the establishment of a dynamic purchasing system (DIO) for the procurement of vehicles under 3.5 tons. The financial plan states that the fleet shall be rolled over within a frame of approx. NOK 4 million per annum. A dynamic procurement system is established to ensure a simple and flexible procurement process. This gives the contracting authority the possibility to hold simplified competitions with a ten day tender deadline for one or several vehicles. This has been requested by actors in the automotive industry, as reservation of cars over several weeks in connection with traditional tender competitions makes it difficult for suppliers to participate. The new scheme gives tenderers a better opportunity to participate, which is expected to give the municipality a better offer. About Dynamic Purchasing System The dynamic purchasing system will be established in accordance with the Public Procurement Regulations (FOA) part I and part III and it will be carried out as a restricted tender contest, cf. the Public Procurement Regulations § 26-5. The scheme is a two-stage procedure: Stage 1: Qualification phase, in which tenderers apply for admission to the scheme. Stage 2: Implementation of mini-competitions, in which qualified tenderers are invited to submit tender offers. A contract will not be signed for admission to the scheme. The contract will only be signed after a completed competition for each procurement. The scheme is fully electronic, and all communication and tender deliveries shall be carried out via the contracting authority ́s competition tool. Tenderers can apply for admission to the scheme by submitting a qualification application with ESPD. The scheme is open for continuous admissions: New suppliers can apply for admission throughout the entire scheme period. Applications are processed continuously All tenderers who fulfil the qualification requirements will be included in the scheme. Description of the delivery The dynamic purchasing system includes the purchase of passenger cars and goods vans. The scheme shall be used for ongoing procurements for the entire duration of the scheme. The estimated value over 10 years is NOK 40 million. It may be necessary to procure both passenger cars and goods vans and the need can vary in regard to i.a. size, capacity and other qualities. Service and follow-up of the vehicles is a part of the delivery. It is therefore a requirement that the tenderer is an authorised branded dealer and has his own workshop approved by the Norwegian Public Roads Administration. Implementation of competitions in the scheme The contracting authority will hold mini-competitions for concrete procurements, in which: All qualified tenderers are invited to submit a tender. The requirement specifications and contract terms will be determined in each competition. The award will be based on the criteria stated in the competition. The award criteria will normally include: Price Technical and functional quality Service and follow-up Delivery time The tender deadline in mini competitions will normally not be shorter than ten days. Other conditions There are requirements for wages and working conditions in accordance with the current rules. The contracting authority reserves the right to reject tenderers who do not fulfil the qualification requirements, or that are covered by the rejection regulations in PPR § 24-2. Information subject to client confidentiality will be processed in accordance with the current rules.

title-proc.eng: Laboratory Testing Services for the National Wastewater Surveillance Programme

description-proc.eng: The Health Protection Surveillance Centre (HPSC) intends to enter into a three-year arrangement with University College Dublin, School of Biomolecular and Biomedical Science (UCD SBBS), for the provision of laboratory testing services including transport of samples for the National Wastewater Surveillance Programme (NWSP) until 31 December 2029. The NWSP was established in 2021 following endorsement by the National Public Health Emergency Team (NPHET) as a national wastewater surveillance system to support public health protection through the monitoring of pathogens and emerging biological threats at population level. The programme is delivered through a partnership involving HPSC, Uisce Éireann, UCD National Virus Reference Laboratory (NVRL) and UCD SBBS. The NWSP provides an early warning system for infectious diseases by monitoring wastewater treatment plants throughout Ireland. Current programme activities include weekly testing for SARS-CoV-2 viral load from 30 wastewater treatment plants and testing for poliovirus types 1, 2 and 3, influenza A and B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) A and B from selected sites. The programme also supports downstream whole genome sequencing activities undertaken by NVRL and contributes to national and international public health surveillance initiatives. The scope of the programme is expected to expand in response to the Recast Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (EU) 2024/3019, which requires Member States to establish coordinated wastewater monitoring systems for public health parameters such as SARS-CoV-2, poliovirus, influenza, emerging pathogens as well as mandatory surveillance of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Future requirements may include additional pathogen testing and will include bacterial culture analysis, AMR gene monitoring, and enhanced reporting obligations. The proposed arrangement will provide laboratory testing, analysis, reporting, maintenance of programme-specific methodologies and continued support for national wastewater surveillance activities. The arrangement will ensure continuity of a critical public health programme while supporting Ireland's preparedness for future public health threats and compliance with emerging European requirements. The arrangement will also include the distribution of wastewater samples from designated wastewater treatment plants which will require UCD to secure transport services under a public tendering process. HPSC intends to award the contract to University College Dublin in accordance with Article 32(2)(b)(ii) of Directive 2014/24/EU. No contract shall be awarded to UCD in respect of these services until a period of fourteen (14) days has elapsed, commencing on day following the publication of this notice in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJEU).

title-proc.eng: Industrial-scale paper and board piloting services at Valmet’s Rautpohja pilot facility

description-proc.eng: THE OBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT VTT procures industrial-scale piloting services for the development, validation, demonstration and scale-up of fibre-based products, production processes and related technologies. The services are used in VTT’s research, development and customer projects when testing at industrially relevant machine speeds, process conditions or equipment configurations is required. The procurement supports the progression of technologies and product concepts from laboratory and VTT pilot-scale validation towards industrial implementation. The piloting may include, for example, trials related to new fibre-based products, raw materials, furnish compositions, chemical applications, multilayer structures, forming concepts, pressing, drying, and other paper and board manufacturing processes. The standard piloting service includes trial planning and preparation, pilot-machine operation, standard operating personnel, process supervision, agreed pilot equipment and facilities, required utilities, standard process measurements and data collection, the trial report, a results review meeting, normal machine cleaning, safety induction and site-access arrangements. The available piloting environment enables, depending on the agreed configuration, trials involving multilayer fibre-based web structures, alternative headbox and forming configurations, different pressing and drying arrangements, and wet-end or web-based application of starch, chemicals and other materials. The procurement covers project-specific pilot trial campaigns carried out at Supplier's pilot facility. LEGAL BASIS FOR DIRECT PROCUREMENT According to the 40 § section 2(2) of the Act on Public Contracts (1397/2016), only a certain supplier can implement the procurement for a technical reason, or for a reason related to protecting an exclusive right; it shall be a further condition that there are no reasonable alternatives or substitute solutions, and that the absence of competition is not due to an artificial narrowing of the terms and conditions of the procurement. The procurement concerns industrial-scale piloting services to be carried out at Valmet Technologies Oy’s Rautpohja pilot facility. The required services must be performed in a specific pilot environment, using dedicated pilot equipment, process configurations and operational capabilities that are uniquely available at the Rautpohja facility. The purpose of the procurement is to enable research, development and innovation projects requiring industrially relevant paper and board manufacturing conditions, including pilot-scale validation, demonstration and scale-up of fibre-based products and processes. The required piloting environment associated technical expertise and operational support form an integrated service that cannot be obtained from an alternative supplier without significant technical limitations and additional costs. For technical reasons, the procurement can only be provided by Valmet Technologies Oy. The required piloting environment, including the specific pilot equipment, process configurations, technical infrastructure and associated operational capabilities, is uniquely available at Valmet Technologies Oy’s Rautpohja pilot facility. No other supplier has access to an equivalent technical environment or is able to provide the required combination of equipment, process conditions, technical expertise and operational support under comparable conditions. Alternative solutions have been considered, but no reasonable substitute capable of meeting the technical requirements of the procurement has been identified. The absence of competition is therefore due to objective technical reasons and not to an artificial restriction of the parameters of the procurement. Accordingly, there is no reasonable alternative or substitute, and the conditions for direct procurement under Section 40(2)(2) of the Finnish Public Procurement Act are fulfilled.

title-proc.nld: Geofysisch onderzoek ter ondersteuning van de exploratie naar kritieke grondstoffen en diepe aardwarmte – Massief van Brabant
title-proc.eng: Geophysical investigation to support exploration for critical raw materials and deep geothermal energy – Brabant Massif

description-proc.nld: Deze opdracht omvat het uitvoeren van gravimetrische en magneto-tellurische metingen in het Massief van Brabant (Vlaanderen), in kader van geologische exploratie naar mineralisaties en diepe geothermie. Tegelijkertijd zal de nieuwe data toelaten om bijkomend inzicht te verwerven in de interne structuur, opbouw en geodynamische geschiedenis van het Brabant Massief. De opdracht focust op twee studiegebieden, en omvat een vast gedeelte en voorwaardelijk gedeelte. Wanneer beslist wordt het voorwaardelijk gedeelte uit te voeren zal dit gebeuren met een schriftelijk bericht van de leidend ambtenaar van deze opdracht. Het eerste studiegebied (ca. 11-16 km²) is gesitueerd in het zuidwesten van Vlaams-Brabant. Dit gebied maakt deel uit van zone 1 van het Vlaams Exploratieprogramma (onderdeel van het Belgisch Exploratieprogramma) Kritieke Grondstoffen: “lagedensiteitslichamen en polysulfidemineralisaties in het Massief van Brabant”. Het studiegebied omvat diverse geologische structuren en kenmerken die relevant zijn voor verdere exploratie, waaronder de Nieuwpoort-Asquempont Fault Zone, het Asquempont Lineament, hypabyssale en mogelijk plutonische intrusies en polysulfidemineralisaties die werden vastgesteld in bestaande boringen. Om structuren en onderlinge relaties beter in kaart te brengen, wordt bijkomend geofysisch onderzoek noodzakelijk geacht alvorens in een volgende fase van het Exploratieprogramma een focusgebied af te bakenen voor verder onderzoek, met potentieel (afhankelijk van de resultaten en beschikbare financiering) het plaatsen van een boring. Meer bepaald dienen er bij deze opdracht bijkomende gravimetrische metingen uitgevoerd te worden ter verfijning van de bestaande data om te komen tot een resolutie van gemiddeld 4 metingen per km2, aangevuld met magneto-tellurische (MT) metingen langs meerdere lijntrajecten doorheen het studiegebied. De gravimetrische metingen en de helft van de MT-metingen vormen het vaste (minimale) gedeelte van dit bestek. De tweede helft van de MT-metingen maken deel uit van het voorwaardelijk gedeelte van dit bestek (meer uitleg in hoofdstuk 3). Een mogelijk tweede studiegebied is gesitueerd in de regio Zuid-West-Vlaanderen. Dit gebied is een zoekzone voor diepe aardwarmte. In deze fase van exploratie is het de bedoeling om met MT-metingen een duidelijker beeld te krijgen van de geologische structuur in het studiegebied, met specifieke aandacht voor de ligging en het eventueel watervoerende karakter van de breukzones. Dit tweede studiegebied maakt integraal deel uit van het voorwaardelijke gedeelte van dit bestek (meer uitleg in hoofdstuk 3). Het uitvoeren van de metingen en de verwerking van de ruwe data tot een interpreteerbaar eindresultaat vormen de kern van deze opdracht. De opdrachtnemer voorziet in een eerste, grootschalige interpretatie van de bekomen resultaten, maar een gedetailleerde interpretatie en de verdere opvolging van het exploratietraject maken geen deel uit van deze opdracht.
description-proc.eng: This contract involves carrying out gravimetric and magnetotelluric measurements in the Brabant Massif (Flanders) as part of geological exploration for mineralisation and deep geothermal energy. At the same time, the new data will provide further insight into the internal structure, composition and geodynamic history of the Brabant Massif. The contract focuses on two study areas and comprises a fixed portion and a conditional portion. If it is decided to proceed with the conditional portion, this will be communicated in writing by the official responsible for the contract. The first study area (approx. 11–16 km²) is located in the south-western part of Flemish Brabant. This area forms part of Zone 1 of the Flemish Exploration Program (part of the Belgian Exploration Program) for Critical Raw Materials: ‘low-density bodies and polysulphide mineralisation in the Brabant Massif’. The study area includes various geological structures and features that are relevant to further exploration, including the Nieuwpoort-Asquempont Fault Zone, the Asquempont Lineament, hypabyssal and possibly plutonic intrusions, and polysulphide mineralisation identified in existing boreholes. To better map the structures and their interrelationships, additional geophysical investigation is considered necessary before defining a focus area for further investigation in the next phase of the Exploration Program, potentially followed by drilling a borehole, depending on the results and available funding. More specifically, under this contract, additional gravimetric measurements are to be carried out to refine the existing data and achieve an average resolution of 4 measurements per km², supplemented by magnetotelluric (MT) measurements along several transects through the study area. The gravimetric measurements and half of the MT measurements constitute the fixed (minimum) portion of these specifications. The second half of the MT measurements forms part of the conditional portion of these specifications (see Chapter 3 for further details). Southern West Flanders is a potential second study area. This area is a prospecting area for deep geothermal energy. At this stage of the exploration, the aim is to use MT measurements to obtain a clearer picture of the geological structure of the study area, with particular attention to the location and potential waterbearing nature of the fault zones. This second study area forms part of the conditional portion of these specifications (see Chapter 3 for further details). Carrying out the measurements and processing the raw data into an interpretable result form the core of this contract. The contractor shall provide an initial, large-scale interpretation of the results obtained, but detailed interpretation and further follow-up of the Exploration Program do not form part of this contract.

title-proc.eng: Pipetting robot - 202511

description-proc.eng: The Norwegian Institute of Marine Research, department Molecular Biology Laboratory in Bergen, shall procure a flexible pipetting robot (liquid handler-robot, LH). The instrument shall be integrated in our production line for genotyping with next-generation sequencing (NGS), which is based on two stage PCR methodology. Thus the instrument will primarily be used for the construction of the NGS libraries and preparation of these for sequencing. The tasks that the instrument shall carry out include: i) Transferring DNA-templat, as well as adding master mixers and primers. ii) Cleaning PCR products (e.g. magnetic bullets) iii) Automated ("hands-off") quantification of DNA iv) Individual normalisation of libraries based on DNA concentration v) Merging of libraries The planned flow is 20,000– 30,000 samples per annum in a sample flow that will normally be carried out in 4 x 96 well plates with a reaction volume of 5-20 uL. In the future we envisage that 384 well plates will be a part of the test flow. As the instrument shall be used post-PCR, it is important that the instrument design allows effective cleaning and thorough decontamination. We would like a quick instrument with high capacity, pipetting precision and accuracy - even at low reaction volumes. In addition the robot is required to have great flexibility and an intuitive user interface, so that applications can be created and modified by personnel without advanced programming competence.
